justification: One authorized data repair on production (DQ-41: null 528 label-derived Jan-1 effective_dates) plus its committed script and tracker close-out. No served rendering path changes - the cohort was already quarantined (basis NULL, never rendered) - so critical tier is not warranted, but a guarded prod UPDATE is above minor.

falsifiable_check.passes_when: The dry-run reports 'already repaired' with Jan-1 basis-NULL cohort 0 and Jan-1 remaining 0 (demonstrated live post-apply: rows=1071, effective_date set=365, Jan-1 remaining=0, written 528 of predicted 528).
falsifiable_check.fails_when: Exit 2 whenever the state diverges from the authorization: cohort not exactly 528 pre-apply, Jan-1 dates carrying a basis (outside the authorization), a pre-existing backup table that cannot roll this run back, a partial apply where written != 528, or DATABASE_URL unset (nothing measured is not a pass).
falsifiable_check.demonstrated_failing: Pre-apply dry-run showed the failing state this repair removes: 528 Jan-1 basis-NULL dates measured live (the migration-040 label-parser cohort, e.g. v2016-current -> 2016-01-01 and v2014-amended-feb-2026 -> 2014-01-01 contradicting its own label). Post-apply re-run plans zero writes.
falsifiable_check.mutation_evidence: Drop the basis-IS-NULL predicate -> a future Jan-1 date WITH a basis would enter the cohort and the count-guard exits 2 against the 528 authorization. Drop the backup-exists abort -> a stale backup table could not roll back this run. Drop the per-row t.effective_date = b.effective_date guard -> a row edited between plan and apply would be silently nulled; with the guard it is skipped and written != 528 exits 2.

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_setback_controls: 1071 rows, 893 effective_date set, 528 exactly Jan-1 with effective_date_basis NULL (measured live this session, twice). dcp_version retained on every row (the source string). dcp_plan_as_at (28 rows) is the precision-honest home for future re-derivation.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: If the cohort had drifted from 528 between authorization and run, the script refuses (exit 2, re-measure). If a Jan-1 date had gained a basis, the cohort predicate excludes it and the 528 assertion catches the count change.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Existing rows only; UPDATE joins the asserted backup table by id with a per-row guard on the exact backed-up date and basis still NULL. No new rows, no other columns touched.

functions.name: main
functions.input: CLI flags --apply and --backup-table plus DATABASE_URL from the environment via dotenv
functions.output: exit 0 on clean dry-run/apply/already-repaired, exit 2 on any divergence or partial apply
functions.if_none: missing DATABASE_URL exits 2 with 'nothing was checked is not a pass'

values.value: cohort count from the live table
values.if_missing: query failure lands in the except arm - rolled back, exit 2

queries.purpose: guarded null of the authorized cohort
queries.where_clause: t.id = b.id AND t.effective_date = b.effective_date AND t.effective_date_basis IS NULL (joined to the asserted 528-row backup)
queries.if_zero: written 0 != 528 -> exit 2, not read as clean
queries.if_wrong: a row changed between plan and apply fails the per-row guard and is skipped, surfacing as a count mismatch

break_it.scenario: the repair is re-run after a successful apply and nulls something else or reports success emptily
break_it.what_happens: a second write pass could hide drift behind an 'already done' message that cannot fail
break_it.how: scripts/repair_dq41_null_label_derived_dates.py:82-101 - cohort 0 proves the intended post-state (0 Jan-1 remaining) before claiming done; Jan-1-with-basis is DIVERGED exit 2. Demonstrated live: post-apply dry-run planned zero writes

break_it.scenario: a future Jan-1 effective_date that carries a real basis (a plan genuinely amended on 1 January) is swept into the null
break_it.what_happens: a legitimate dated row would lose its date under a repair authorized only for the unattributed cohort
break_it.how: COHORT_WHERE requires effective_date_basis IS NULL and the UPDATE re-checks it per row at write time
break_it.repro: SQL: a row with effective_date='2027-01-01', effective_date_basis='stated_in_document' does not match COHORT_WHERE

break_it.scenario: a backup table left over from an earlier partial run silently absorbs the CREATE and cannot roll back this run
break_it.what_happens: the printed rollback would restore stale values from a different run's pre-state
break_it.how: scripts/repair_dq41_null_label_derived_dates.py:113-121 - existing backup table aborts before any UPDATE with instructions to pass a fresh --backup-table
break_it.repro: re-running with --apply after success returns via the cohort-0 path first; with a fresh cohort the exists-check aborts before any UPDATE

post_merge.manual_verify: No - repair already applied and verified live (528/528, 365 dates remain, 0 Jan-1, 1071 rows intact); backup dcp_setback_controls_dq41_null_20260803 retained
